The example works fine in the foreground. So the problem is specific to the "no paths positive demand" input. That input triggers an infinite loop or a hang in the planner.

And the "process gone at t=3s with no output" earlier is confusing... Oh! Maybe the process was killed by the CPU limit? No, 3s.

Hmm, wait. In hangtest2.sh I did NOT use `timeout`, so the planner ran with stdout redirected to a file. The process "is gone" after 3s with no output. That means it exited (or died) without output. But in the foreground it hangs forever.

The difference: in the background case, stdin was redirected from the file too... identical.

Unless the process was killed by the kernel OOM killer or RLIMIT_AS... Let me check the exit code properly with a script that writes to files (no tool pipe involvement).

Let me write a small Python driver that runs the planner with subprocess and a timeout, capturing everything, and writes results to a file. Then read the file.

arguments.command:
cd /app/work && cat > drv.py <<'EOF'
import subprocess, sys, time, json
data = open('/app/work/oneshot.jsonl','rb').read()
t0=time.time()
try:
    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable,'/app/submission/planner.py'], input=data, capture_output=True, timeout=30)
    res = ("rc", p.returncode, "%.2f"%(time.time()-t0), p.stdout[:200], p.stderr[:2000])
except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
    res = ("TIMEOUT", None, "%.2f"%(time.time()-t0), (e.stdout or b'')[:200], (e.stderr or b'')[:2000])
open('/app/work/drv.out','w').write(repr(res))
EOF
timeout 60 python3 drv.py; echo "shell rc=$?"; cat drv.out
